title: Sebastian and the Orbit
premise: Odile Dravenmoor, a nonbinary insurance investigator who has spent a decade making themselves small aboard the cargo hauler Sebastian, intercepts a distress beacon in Vessic—a language officially extinct since the Callisto Purges. Following it to the derelict station Meridian's Rest, they find evidence of a massacre that every corporate and governmental record insists never happened, erased so thoroughly that proving it means unproving their own carefully constructed anonymity. As Odile digs, they discover the purge was orchestrated by the very consortium that insures their ship, and that their estranged sister, a records archivist, helped write the false history. Torn between loyalty to family, crew, and truth, Odile broadcasts the recovered archive at devastating personal cost; the book ends with the massacre acknowledged, Odile stripped of their license but finally visible—named in the historical record as the one who refused to let two hundred thousand dead stay deleted.
about_author: Casper Halloran is the pen name of a former maritime insurance adjuster who spent six years investigating 'impossible' losses before turning to fiction. They write from a houseboat off the coast of Maine, where they collect obsolete radio equipment and answer distress signals on frequencies no one else monitors.

chapters.title: Dead Frequencies
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A routine claims audit aboard the hauler Sebastian establishes their meticulous invisibility—false names, scrubbed manifests, a life built on being forgettable. Then the ship's array catches a repeating signal in Vessic, a language extinct for two centuries. Emotional beat: quiet dread as the past knocks on a door Odile welded shut.

chapters.title: The Language of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Flashbacks reveal Odile learned Vessic from their grandmother, a Purge survivor who made them promise never to speak it aloud. The signal repeats a single phrase: 'We are still here.' Odile logs it as interference—but doesn't delete it. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into compulsion.

chapters.title: Cargo and Consequence
chapters.summary: Crew POV—engineer Tam Okafor notices Odile rerouting power to the comms array and covers for them without asking why. Establishes the found-family dynamic: four crew members who ask no questions because they all have pasts. Emotional beat: warmth shadowed by mutual secrets.

chapters.title: Meridian's Rest
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Following triangulated coordinates, the Sebastian finds a station that appears on no chart, hull scarred by weapons fire, airlocks sealed from the inside. Two hundred years of vacuum silence. Emotional beat: awe tipping into horror.

chapters.title: What the Vacuum Keeps
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Inside, Odile finds preserved bodies—not killed by decompression but executed, arranged in the station's central hall. A child's handprint in frozen condensation spells a word in Vessic: REMEMBER. Emotional beat: grief arriving like a physical blow.

chapters.title: Paperwork for the Dead
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, professional mode as armor. Odile begins documenting everything with an investigator's rigor—timestamps, ballistics, registry numbers—because proof is the only prayer they know. But the station's own logs are wiped clean. Someone got here first. Emotional beat: cold fury under clinical calm.

chapters.title: The Consortium's Long Arm
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV—Assessor Corvel of the Halcyon Consortium reviews an automated anomaly flag: an unregistered vessel lingering near a blacklisted coordinate. He dispatches a 'compliance tender' with quiet, bureaucratic menace. Emotional beat: banal evil, patient as paperwork.

chapters.title: Sister Static
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Desperate for records access, Odile swallows pride and contacts their estranged sister Maren, now a senior archivist at the Concordance Records Bureau. Their last conversation ended with Maren reporting Odile's desertion. Maren answers—and warns them to stop digging. Emotional beat: old wounds reopened by new fear.

chapters.title: Ten Years Invisible
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam confronts Odile about the detour, and Odile confesses partially—the signal, the language, not the massacre. Tam reveals their own buried history: they fled a conscription draft and understand erasure intimately. Emotional beat: fragile trust deepening into alliance.

chapters.title: The Backup Nobody Burned
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. In the station's maintenance levels, Odile finds a jury-rigged data vault—a technician hid a full backup of Meridian's Rest's records before dying. It's encrypted in Vessic verse-forms only a native speaker could parse. Emotional beat: hope arriving disguised as homework.

chapters.title: Deciphering the Dead
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, intimate and slow. Decryption becomes communion: Odile reads the station's final weeks—births, arguments, a wedding, then the arrival of ships flying Concordance colors. Emotional beat: the dead becoming people, which makes the crime unbearable.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Thousand Names
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The vault holds the full census: 214,806 residents of Meridian's Rest, all listed as 'relocated' in official history. Cross-referencing reveals the relocation ships never existed. Emotional beat: vertigo—how do you mourn a number this large?

chapters.title: Compliance
chapters.summary: Corvel's POV. The compliance tender boards a neutral port and quietly buys information about the Sebastian. Corvel's method is revealed: he doesn't destroy evidence, he reclassifies it until it means nothing. Emotional beat: dread through competence.

chapters.title: Maren's Ledger
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. We see her side: she discovered the falsified Purge records years ago, reported it, and was promoted instead of listened to. She warned Odile not to protect them—or herself. Her loyalty is to the archive, not the family. Emotional beat: sympathy complicating antagonism.

chapters.title: The Insurance Angle
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, investigator's epiphany. The Sebastian is insured by Halcyon—which means Halcyon can void their coverage, seize the ship, and legally strand the crew anywhere. The massacre wasn't just hidden; it was underwritten. Emotional beat: realizing the enemy owns your lifeline.

chapters.title: Running Dark
chapters.summary: Pilot Sefa's POV. Sefa takes the Sebastian off-grid, threading unpatrolled debris fields while Odile sleeps in shifts beside the decrypted archive. Crew tension: navigator Pell wants to sell the data and disappear; Tam refuses. Emotional beat: the family fracturing under weight.

chapters.title: What Pell Knows
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. Flashback: Pell lost family in a smaller, quieter cover-up and took consortium money once before. Selling out Odile would be survival; betraying them would be repetition. Emotional beat: temptation rendered sympathetic.

chapters.title: The Verse-Keys
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The deepest encryption layer requires spoken Vessic—voice-authenticated by cadence patterns only native speakers carry. Odile must speak aloud the language they promised their grandmother to bury. Emotional beat: breaking a deathbed vow to honor what the vow protected.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Voice
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, memory chapter. Full flashback to childhood: lullabies in Vessic, the grandmother's stories of Meridian's Rest before the Purges, her insistence that forgetting is how killers win twice. Odile understands at last why she taught them. Emotional beat: inheritance reframed as assignment.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Action chapter, rotating crew POVs. The compliance tender corners the Sebastian in a fuel depot. A tense standoff resolved by Sefa's reckless slingshot maneuver and Tam venting cargo to change their mass signature. They escape, barely, flagged and hunted. Emotional beat: adrenaline giving way to the knowledge there's nowhere left to hide.

chapters.title: Casualties of Proof
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The escape cost them their transponder legitimacy; every port will deny them docking. Odile offers the crew a chance to bail out at a neutral station. No one takes it. Even Pell stays. Emotional beat: belonging chosen explicitly for the first time.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Bargain
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren secretly verifies a fragment of Odile's data against sealed originals and confirms it's genuine. She contacts Odile with an offer: she'll authenticate the archive publicly if Odile brings it to the Bureau—but the Bureau answers to Halcyon money. Emotional beat: hope that smells like a trap.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for a Massacre
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Decrypted fleet orders reveal the Purge was rehearsed at Meridian's Rest as a template—methodology later refined and reused on three other stations, all also 'relocated.' The crime isn't historical; it's serial. Emotional beat: scale transforming grief into resolve.

chapters.title: Corvel's File on Dravenmoor
chapters.summary: Corvel's POV. Corvel has assembled Odile's true identity—desertion, aliases, the sister connection. He sends Maren a message: deliver her sibling or become a co-conspirator in 'historical falsification.' Emotional beat: the trap closing on both siblings at once.

chapters.title: Sisters at Airlock's Edge
chapters.summary: Dual POV, Odile and Maren meeting covertly on a mining platform. First face-to-face in ten years. Maren confesses she reported Odile's desertion to save them from a worse charge; Odile admits running was also abandonment. Neither apologizes fully; both understand more. Emotional beat: reconciliation without resolution.

chapters.title: The Broadcast Problem
chapters.summary: Crew council scene, all POVs briefly. Broadcasting the archive needs a high-gain array on a major relay—suicide while flagged. Pell proposes the unthinkable: use Halcyon's own emergency broadcast channel, hijackable for ninety seconds during their quarterly shareholders' address. Emotional beat: audacity born of desperation.

chapters.title: Ninety Seconds
chapters.summary: Planning chapter, Odile's POV. The plan: infiltrate the relay station Kepler Deep during the shareholder address, splice the archive into the feed, and let 214,806 voices interrupt the quarterly report. Every detail planned; every detail likely wrong. Emotional beat: calm before catastrophe.

chapters.title: Kepler Deep
chapters.summary: Infiltration, alternating Odile and Sefa POVs. They enter the relay disguised as maintenance contractors. Security is tighter than intel suggested; Tam creates a diversion that gets him detained. Emotional beat: the plan bleeding in real time.

chapters.title: Diversion and Detention
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Interrogated in a holding room, Tam stalls with bureaucratic nonsense, buying minutes. Corvel arrives personally, recognizes the pattern, and realizes the target is the broadcast—not the vault. Emotional beat: sacrifice measured in seconds.

chapters.title: Splice
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, climax begins. At the console, Odile injects the archive into the live feed. For ninety seconds, every screen in inhabited space shows Meridian's Rest's final hours—names scrolling, voices speaking Vessic, the child's handprint. Emotional beat: triumph and terror simultaneously.

chapters.title: The Whole Sky Watching
chapters.summary: Montage chapter, many brief POVs: dockworkers, students, a Halcyon shareholder, a Purge survivor's descendant recognizing a family name. The lie cracks publicly. Corvel orders a shutdown; the shutdown itself becomes news. Emotional beat: the dead, seen at last.

chapters.title: Retribution, Properly Filed
chapters.summary: Corvel's POV turning inward. With exposure imminent, Halcyon's board designates Corvel the fall figure—he is audited, indicted, erased by the same machinery he served. Emotional beat: the eraser erased; justice arriving sideways.

chapters.title: Aftermath Aboard the Sebastian
chapters.summary: Crew POV. The Sebastian drifts dark, engines cold, awaiting whatever comes. Tam released in the chaos rejoins; Pell confesses his old betrayal to the crew and is met not with forgiveness but with continuation—they need him, and he stays anyway. Emotional beat: grace as practical choice.

chapters.title: Hearing
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Summoned before a Concordance tribunal, Odile testifies—not as investigator but as witness, speaking Vessic on the record for the first time in two centuries of official silence. Maren authenticates the archive publicly, ending her career at the Bureau and beginning something truer. Emotional beat: testimony as homecoming.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The tribunal voids Odile's license, fines them into debt, and formally acknowledges the Meridian's Rest Massacre—both outcomes delivered in the same breath. Justice incomplete, but real. Odile walks out owning nothing except the truth and the crew waiting outside. Emotional beat: costly vindication.

chapters.title: Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. At a memorial on rebuilt Meridian's Rest, survivors' descendants and strangers read the census aloud in shifts—it takes eleven days. Odile reads the name of the technician who saved the backup, and the child who wrote REMEMBER. Emotional beat: mourning as communal act.

chapters.title: Maren's New Archive
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren founds an independent records collective dedicated to auditing 'relocation' histories, recruiting archivists disillusioned with the Bureau. She asks Odile to consult. Sibling rivalry softens into partnership. Emotional beat: repair as ongoing work.

chapters.title: The Weight of Visibility
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Fame sits badly: interviews, documentaries, strangers claiming kinship with their story. Odile struggles to exist loudly after a decade of practice disappearing. A quiet scene with Tam about learning to be known. Emotional beat: identity as adjustment, not arrival.

chapters.title: Still Here
chapters.summary: Final Odile POV. A year later, the Sebastian runs honest cargo under Odile's real name. A faint signal flickers on an old frequency—one word in Vessic, from somewhere far out: 'Still here.' Odile smiles, logs it properly, and answers. Emotional beat: peace earned, vigilance kept, belonging found.

chapters.title: Epilogue: The Investigator of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Distant third-person POV, pulling back. Historians will cite the Dravenmoor Broadcast as the moment the Concordance's founding myth broke. Somewhere between chapters of a new history book, a footnote credits an insurance investigator who proved an impossible accident. Emotional beat: legacy—small, accurate, enough.
